cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a pair of feathered arm bustles (dance regalia) with mirrored, sequinned centers — a type of ceremonial ornament used in Pueblo social dances, consistent with Tewa (Rio Grande Pueblo) use, though not distinguishable from other Pueblo peoples' regalia.

physical.title: regalia; arm-ornament (bustles)
physical.summary: Feathered arm bustles.  Each bustle is constructed of three layers of cardboard discs, which are decorated and layered, the smaller on a larger, the larger mounted on the largest; and attached with shoelaces threaded through the three disc layers; the shoelaces are also used to tie the bustles onto the arm.  The smallest top layer disc is constructed of a central mirror in the centre of variously coloured sequins (silver, black, purple, red, orange, yellow, white and green) surrounded by a circle layer of fuzzy feathers.  the intermediate disc has stiff cut black feathers.  The largest disc has fuzzy and stiff white feathers.   Part of an ensemble of powwow regalia.
